newsitem.title: USA: U.S. medical group seeks tax for research.
newsitem.headline: U.S. medical group seeks tax for research.

text.p: A new group of doctors and scientists Tuesday launched a campaign for a tax on health insurance to support medical research in an era of cost-cutting.

Managed care and other cost-conscious insurance and health care arrangements have squeezed some medical schools and teaching hospitals, who have to compete with other health care facilities that do not do costly research.
A two percent tax on health premiums would raise about $4 billion a year for academic programmes, said the new advocacy group that calls itself Citizens for Public Research.

In the last few years of debate over health reform and Medicare reform there have been various proposals to create taxes or fees to help fund medical education and science research but none has made its way into law.

"The American public has not been informed about the devastating effects the transition to managed care is having on medical research and teaching," said Dr. James Muller, a medical professor at the University of Kentucky and a founder of the group.
